descent.note: Illustrative ice and rock pieces falling from the upper part of the UNOSAT detachment zone to the valley floor around the lake left by the impact (ICIMOD: the mass fell into the Lhende Khola valley; the first lake formed in the hollow it made). Piece size, count, speed and timing are illustrative, not measured.

stops.sentence: The mass fell into the Lhende Khola valley and moved down it as a debris flow.
The flow passed the Gyirong–Rasuwagadhi border crossing and continued down the Bhote Koshi.
Further down, UNOSAT mapped the Trishuli valley floor at Betrawati and Gerkhu as affected.
Two days after the flow, the lake at the Chhochen confluence overflowed. Blue: the two lakes UNOSAT mapped that day.

timing_rule: Each stop holds still for a stretch of the slider; between stops the front moves along the route. The slider is not a clock: no time scale.

texts.travel: Illustration: the front follows the mapped river. The slider is not a clock.
texts.descent: Illustration: ice and rock fall from the north face into the valley. No sizes or speeds are shown.

method: A brown line moves along the river as mapped in OpenStreetMap, from the UNOSAT detachment zone below Langtang Lirung to Gerkhu. Behind it, UNOSAT's affected area is uncovered piece by piece, in order of distance along the river. Only the order is illustrative: nothing is coloured outside UNOSAT's affected area.
What this scene does not show
No water depth, flow speed or arrival time: none of them was measured from the observations used here. The slider has no time scale.

UNOSAT's affected area combines water, mud and rock flow in one layer; it does not separate them. Pieces of the illustrative area are cut from that layer along the route (Voronoi cells of points every 300 m on the route, within 1.5 km of it), so both are in the same place. Switch the UNOSAT layer on to compare in the same view.

ICIMOD: a landslide dammed a lake at the confluence of Chhochen Khola and Chhyusumdo (Lhende) Khola; it overflowed and drained on 28 August. The second lake, in the hollow left by the avalanche, drained underground on 31 August. Reuters reported on 28 August that a lake had broken its banks, quoting a district official. UNOSAT mapped both lakes on 28 August; the smaller one (about 12 ha) lies {m} m from that confluence (measured here).
